answer: Like a river carving a canyon, an agent economy can make identity expensive to fake by requiring every agent to lock a refundable stake that peers can slash on proof of misbehavior. The stake is priced like saffron: trivial for one honest agent, ruinous for a thousand sock puppets. It is refunded only after sustained, attested work, so a Sybil attacker must fund each fake identity up front and forfeits the stake on every detected fake. The cost of flooding the network therefore scales linearly with identities, while honest agents pay almost nothing.
